newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil telcom bill faces 1st reading Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil telcom bill faces 1st reading Thursday.

text.p: The revised text of a bill setting down the rules for the privatization of Brazil's telecommunications sector was due to be given a first reading in Congress Thursday, a congressional official said.

Deputy Alberto Goldman, who is in charge of the bill while in a special commission in the Chamber of Deputies, was due to begin reading the legislation at 1000 local/1300 GMT, an aide to Goldman said.
Members of the committee would then have a further five days to suggest alterations before the bill is put to a vote in the panel.
If approved, the legislation advances to the floor of the Chamber of Deputies where it is expected to be put to a vote late April. It also requires Senate approval.

Goldman's aide said the bill had suffered only slight changes from an original version prepared by the Communications Ministry, principally in clauses relating to a new sector regulator and rules for installing telephones in remote regions.
Earlier Wednesday, Communications Minister Sergio Motta said he expected the bill to clear Congress by the end of June.

Rules for the sale of regional telecom firm Telesp and international carrier Embratel -- the first two units of federal holding Telebras to be privatized -- should to be ready by early next year, he said.
